newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 5.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- Chemical warfare programme founder Wouter Basson, who was arrested for allegedly selling Ecstasy tablets, testified in a bail application behind closed doors yesterday "in the interests of state security".
- Government proposals for a new water supply policy, detailed in a document released yesterday, are intended to produce a national framework and make way for the setting up of regional utilities.
- Merrill Lynch would buy the remaining 49% of Smith Borkum Hare's share capital, giving the US securities firm full ownership of the brokerage, the companies announced last night.

- The glitch-ridden KwaZulu-Natal legislature got off to a chaotic new year start yesterday when politicans who solemnly pledged allegiance to the new constitution discovered they had sworn the wrong oath.
BUSINESS REPORT

- Gold touched an intraday high of $347.05 yesterday as market sentiment was buoyed by reports that Europe's central banks had been forbidden from using gold sale proceeds to reduce government deficits.
- First-half earnings of Iscor plunged 68 percent because of a weak steel market and operational difficulties, the company said yesterday.
- The new tax on interest income of pension funds, as proposed by the Katz commission and implemented in last year's Budget, is proving to be a disappointing source of income for the government.

- A large international consortium had offered to buy the massive pile of confiscated textiles and clothing piling up in customs warehouses, ship it to Europe under customs supervision and guarantee it would not find its way back to South Africa, industry sources said yesterday.
SAKE BEELD
- Iscor's earnings for the six months in December had slumped 66% from 501 million rand to 170 million rand.
- Rand Merchant Bank (RAB) a wholly owned subsidiary of Momentum Life listed group of Rand Merchant Bank lifted its attrbutable earnings in the six months to December 31 to R60 million.
- Merrill Lynch, one of the worlds largest investment consultants, is now the sole proprietor of Smith Borkum Hare.
THE STAR

- A second medical doctor had been arrested in connection with alleged trade in Ecstasy tablets, as Pretoria heart specialist Dr Wouter Basson, arrested last week after allegedly handing 1 000 Ecstasy tablets to a buyer for R60,000, appeared in court yesterday.

- A top-secret destabilisation campaign is allegedly being waged by an elite group of 38 former and present political leaders, bankers, businessmen and some prominent rightwingers to gain economic power and take political control by the year 2004.
- Dismissed South African Football Association executive president Solomon "Stix" Morewa will receive a severance package of more that R250,000.
- Three men, arrested by police after a wild gunbattle in a Johannesburg suburb claimed the lives of two men and left two other wounded, are expected to appear in an identity parade today.
